Uncanny

/un-KAN-ee/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Uncanny means strange or mysterious in an unsettling way, as if touched by something beyond normal explanation.

Uncanny means strange or mysterious in an unsettling way, as if touched by something beyond normal explanation. There was something uncanny about the antique doll in the shop window; no matter where visitors stood, its painted eyes seemed to follow them across the room.

Worked Example

Long after the twins had been assigned to cabins on opposite ends of the lake, their camp counselors kept noticing something uncanny: the girls would start humming the same tune at the same moment, as if some invisible signal passed between them across the water.

The twins' perfectly matched behavior feels mysterious and a little unsettling, beyond ordinary coincidence, which is what makes it uncanny.

How Uncanny Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

eerie

eerie: strange in a frightening, ghostly way

unnerving

unnerving: causing someone to lose their calm

otherworldly

otherworldly: seeming to belong beyond the natural world

Antonyms

ordinary

ordinary: normal and unremarkable

natural

natural: easily explained by everyday causes

How Strong Is It? — odd → uncanny → supernatural

odd vs. uncanny

odd vs. uncanny: Something odd is merely a bit strange, while something uncanny is strange in a way that raises the hairs on the back of your neck.

supernatural vs. uncanny

supernatural vs. uncanny: An uncanny event feels almost beyond explanation, but a supernatural one openly breaks the laws of nature.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — un-

Prefix — un-: not

Root — canny

Root — canny: from Scots canny, knowing, shrewd, from an old Germanic root meaning to know

Put it together

Put it together: Uncanny joins un-, 'not,' to canny, a Scots word meaning 'knowing, shrewd, safe to deal with,' from an ancient Germanic root meaning 'to know.' Something uncanny is literally 'beyond what can be known,' strange in a way that ordinary knowledge cannot explain.

Use the root in a new word: canny

Use the root in a new word: canny: The canny shopkeeper always knew exactly which antiques would sell, showing the same 'knowing' root that hides inside uncanny.

Word Choice

neutral

Uncanny describes strangeness with an unsettling, almost supernatural edge, as in 'an uncanny resemblance' or 'an uncanny ability.' Save it for things that give you a small shiver; something that is merely different or quirky is not uncanny.
